schemaVersion.description: Semver of the capability-artifact contract this document was written against. A loader accepts only the version it was built for; a mismatch is rejected rather than guessed at.

id.description: Capability id: a lowercase kebab-case slug, e.g. "member-lookup". Stable across artifact versions.

version.description: Version of this capability. Bump major when params/outputs change incompatibly, minor for new optional params/outputs, patch for locator or checkpoint fixes.

does.description: What the capability does in the target app, in one or two sentences, including its side effects.

needs.description: What the caller must supply (params) and what is resolved at run time (credentials).

returns.description: What a success returns, and which business outcomes the caller should expect.

summary.description: Plain-language contract for a reviewer and a calling agent (R2.7).

vendorApp.description: Vendor application id: a lowercase kebab-case slug naming the legacy product, e.g. "coreone". Independent of the tenant.

variant.description: Tenant/variant id: a lowercase kebab-case slug naming one institution's deployment of a vendor app, e.g. "tenant-a". Tenants of the same app can differ in labels and layout (R7.2).

appVersion.description: The app version observed during discovery, e.g. "CoreOne 7.4".

app.description: The app and tenant this capability was discovered against. Deliberately no origin: routes are relative, and the origin comes from the app profile/CLI at run time, so the artifact never pins an environment.

baseId.description: Id of the base capability this one overrides.

extends.description: Reserved for a base-plus-tenant-overrides design (R7.2/S5): this artifact is a variant of the named base. Recorded only; no v1 engine reads it.

anyOf.description: Run id: "<kind>-<yyyymmddThhmmss>-<4hex>" with kind discovery|replay and a UTC timestamp, e.g. "replay-20260929T101500-a1b2". Names the run evidence directory.

discoveryRunId.description: The discovery run this artifact was compiled from (its evidence directory); null = hand-written.

compiledAt.description: When the artifact was compiled (ISO 8601, UTC).

compilerVersion.description: Version of the compiler that produced the artifact.

model.description: Id of the model that drove discovery, e.g. "claude-sonnet-4-5" — the id only, never a prompt or transcript. null = no model (hand-written).

items.description: Step id: "s<NN>-<slug>", e.g. "s03-click-search". Assigned once by the compiler and kept stable when steps are edited or inserted, so evidence, drift reports and outcome-rule scopes keep pointing at the same step.

humanStepIds.description: Steps recorded from a human operator during a handoff rather than chosen by the model.

provenance.description: Where the artifact came from. Kept separate from the model transcript, which is never stored here.

credentialRef.description: The one credential this capability signs on with. Every credential value in the steps must reference it; omitted = the capability uses no credential.

name.description: Parameter name: a camelCase identifier, e.g. "memberId". Referenced from templates as {{memberId}}.

description.description: What the caller must supply, written for a calling agent and a reviewer (R2.7).

pattern.description: ECMAScript regular expression the whole value must match (implicitly anchored with ^…$).

oneOf.description: Free text, optionally constrained by a full-match pattern and length bounds.
A safe integer. As a param it may arrive as a digit string (CLI) and is coerced to a number.

scale.description: Maximum number of fractional digits, e.g. 2 for a currency amount.

oneOf.description: An exact decimal, always represented as a string matching ^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$ with at most `scale` fractional digits (e.g. "1234.56"). Never a JSON number, to avoid floating-point loss on money.
true/false. As a param the strings "true"/"false" are accepted and coerced.

values.description: The allowed values, e.g. the option values of a dropdown.

oneOf.description: One of a fixed set of strings.
An ISO 8601 calendar date string "YYYY-MM-DD".

type.description: The value vocabulary shared by params and outputs, discriminated on `kind`.

required.description: Whether the caller must supply it. Defaults to true.

sensitive.description: Whether the value is sensitive (PII, account data). Defaults to true: sensitive values are redacted in every sink and can never be stored as literals or examples.

example.description: A synthetic example value. Forbidden when `sensitive` is true; must match `type`.

items.description: A typed input of the capability. Steps reference it as {"kind":"param"} or {{name}}.

name.description: Output name: a camelCase identifier, e.g. "savingsBalance". Keys the success result outputs record.

items.description: A typed output of the capability, produced by exactly one extract step and returned on success.

outputs.description: Typed outputs returned on success; names are unique and each is extracted exactly once.

steps.description: The deterministic steps, in order: login-phase steps first, then main steps. Ids are unique.

successCondition.description: Verified after the last step; the run is a success only if it holds (and every output validated).

outcomeRules.description: Runtime conditions specific to this capability; they override app-profile defaults by code.

contentHash.description: "sha256:<64 lowercase hex>" over the canonical JSON of the artifact with contentHash excluded (keys sorted recursively). Detects any edit to a persisted artifact.

description: A capability artifact: a typed, versioned, deterministic program compiled from a successful discovery run and replayed with no model in the loop. Stores parameter references, never the concrete values used during discovery.

id.description: Step id: "s<NN>-<slug>", e.g. "s03-click-search". Assigned once by the compiler and kept stable when steps are edited or inserted, so evidence, drift reports and outcome-rule scopes keep pointing at the same step.

description.description: What the step does and why, written for a reviewer and an operator (R2.7), e.g. "Click Search to look up the member". Never contains a concrete param value.

phase.description: login: part of signing on (re-run once on session expiry); main: the capability itself. Login steps come first.

risk.description: Risk class recorded by the compiler. Replay recomputes it from policy and takes the max of the two, so an edited artifact can never lower the risk of a step.

checkpoint.description: The condition verified after the action. Required for screen-changing kinds (navigate, click, press, select, dismiss_dialog) — invariant 5.

timeoutMs.description: Upper bound for resolving the target and performing the action; omitted = the engine default.

route.description: A route relative to the app origin, starting with "/", e.g. "/member/detail?m={{memberId}}". The origin is supplied at run time by the app profile, so the same artifact runs against any environment of the app and never carries a host name.

oneOf.description: Load a route of the app (relative to the origin supplied at run time) in the top document.

Checkpoint.description: A verifiable condition on the screen. Every screen-changing step is followed by one (invariant 5): "the click did not throw" is not success. Uses signals any surface can provide.

description.description: Human-readable name of the target, e.g. "Search button in the member search form". Shown to operators and in failure reports.

ladder.description: Locator rungs in stability order (most stable first). The resolver tries each in turn inside `frame`; resolving on a later rung succeeds but is reported as drift.

TargetRef.description: A UI element the artifact acts on or checks, independent of any one selector technology.

oneOf.description: Preferred hop. Legacy framesets address frames by name (target="content"), so the name is part of the app wiring and survives layout and URL changes.

glob.description: Glob over the frame document URL path, e.g. "**/member/*.jsp".

oneOf.description: Fallback hop for unnamed frames: matches the frame by the path of the document it shows.

title.description: The frame `title` attribute or its document title.

oneOf.description: Fallback hop when neither name nor URL is stable.

items.description: One step down the frame tree.

FrameScope.description: Ordered frame path from the top document to the document that holds the target; [] means the top document. On a non-web surface this names the window/pane path instead.

exact.description: true: the name must match exactly. Omitted/false: case-insensitive substring.

rationale.description: Why this rung identifies the target robustly (R2.3): which stable property it relies on and what change would break it.

surface.description: Surface-tagged extras. Informational: the resolver never uses them as a primary rung, so the core rung stays expressible on a desktop surface (R7.1).

cssHint.description: A CSS selector recorded for diagnostics and drift reports only.

LocatorRung.description: One rung of the locator ladder. Rungs are tried in order and the first unique match wins. A visual-anchor rung (image/OCR match) is a design-only extension for non-DOM surfaces and is not part of v1.

name.description: The declared param whose run-time value is used.

oneOf.description: The value of a declared capability parameter, supplied by the caller at run time.

value.description: The constant value. Must be non-sensitive.

oneOf.description: A constant baked into the artifact (e.g. an option value "savings"). Only for non-sensitive values: a step that marks its value sensitive refuses a literal (enforced by the step schema), so discovered PII can never be stored here.

ref.description: Name of a credential held outside the artifact (resolved at run time from the environment/secret store), e.g. "mockbank-operator". It is a reference, never the secret itself.

field.description: Which part of the referenced credential to use.

oneOf.description: A field of a credential resolved at run time from outside the artifact. The secret is never stored.

ValueExpr.description: The only way a step carries a value: a param reference, a non-sensitive literal, or a credential reference.

code.description: Outcome/condition code: snake_case, e.g. "member_not_found". Stable; calling agents branch on it.

class.description: How a recognised condition is handled. business_outcome: a valid answer returned to the caller (e.g. member_not_found), never a failure. recoverable: handled inside the run by a bounded recovery and logged, never returned. failure: the run stops with evidence (or escalates to a human).

description.description: What the condition means for the caller and the reviewer (R2.7).

text.description: Text that appears on the screen when the condition holds, e.g. "No records match your search criteria".

frame.description: Frame to look in; omitted = any frame.

oneOf.description: The condition shows a fixed message somewhere on the screen.

signatures.description: Leaf signatures; the condition holds when at least one matches. any_of cannot be nested.

oneOf.description: Any of several signals identifies the condition (e.g. a title OR a body text).

signature.description: How a runtime condition is recognised from an observation, discriminated on `kind`. Evaluated deterministically by replay; no model is involved.

anyOf.description: The rule is checked before and after every step.

items.description: Step id: "s<NN>-<slug>", e.g. "s03-click-search". Assigned once by the compiler and kept stable when steps are edited or inserted, so evidence, drift reports and outcome-rule scopes keep pointing at the same step.

anyOf.description: The rule is checked only around these steps (e.g. not-found only after the Search click).

message.description: Element whose text becomes the result message. The text passes the redaction layer before it reaches any sink; omitted = the description is used.

recovery.description: Required when class is recoverable; forbidden otherwise.

oneOf.description: Close the recognised native dialog, then continue the current step.

target.description: The control that closes the interstitial, e.g. a "Continue" link.

max.description: Maximum number of retries of the current step. Always bounded.

backoffMs.description: Delay before each retry, in milliseconds.

oneOf.description: Re-run the current step (e.g. after a failed load). Never used for an irreversible step.
Sign on again: re-run the login-phase steps once, then the main steps up to the current one. Refused (session_lost) if an irreversible step already ran.

OutcomeRule.description: Recognises one runtime condition and says how it is classified and handled. Resolution order at replay: artifact rule, then app profile default, then engine catalog default.
